acceptance_criteria.criterion: normaliseRepo() maps CredentialId to credentialId in the normalised repository object.
The repository detail view (#/repositories/:id) shows a "Credential" section with a <select> dropdown.
The dropdown is populated from GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options with options: "None" + each matching credential displayed as label (host).
When exactly one credential matches (auto-selected), it is pre-selected in the dropdown with an "(auto)" indicator.
When a stored CredentialId exists, the corresponding credential is pre-selected in the dropdown.
Changing the dropdown selection calls PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential to persist the choice.
The repository list view table shows a credential status indicator for each repository row.
The project-detail view's buildRepositoriesSection() repository table shows the same credential status indicator.
api.repositories.updateCredential(id, credentialId) sends PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential with the correct body.
All GUI tests for normalise.test.mjs, repository-detail.test.mjs, repositories.test.mjs, and api.config.test.mjs pass.

comments.note: repository-detail.js buildCredentialSection() uses a fire-and-forget async IIFE pattern (calling api.repositories.credentialOptions inside .then chains attached to a synchronously-returned section element). This is consistent with the existing loadWorkspaceRows pattern in the same file, but a future refactor could use an async helper that returns the section after the fetch resolves, reducing the need for internal DOM mutation post-render.

The credential status badge in repositories.js and project-detail.js uses an emoji (🔑) as the 'set' indicator. While visually clear, emoji rendering can vary across platforms and screen readers. A CSS-based icon or text badge (e.g. 'Set') with a consistent aria-label would be more accessible and easier to style.

normalise.js has no tests for normaliseRepo() for its core fields (id, name, url, LastRefreshedAt) — only the new CredentialId mapping is tested. The existing AC tests for the views implicitly exercise normaliseRepo() but dedicated unit tests for all fields would improve isolation. Out of scope for this WP but worth noting.

comments.note: api.repositories.updateCredential(id, credentialId) uses JSON.stringify({ credentialId }) — if called with undefined (not in the current UI code path), JSON.stringify silently strips the key, producing {} body instead of { credentialId: '' }. Not a real bug (UI always passes a string from select.value), but defensive input validation (throw if credentialId is not a string) would harden the contract.

The auto-select logic (line 116 of repository-detail.js) requires exactly one option AND auto=true. If the backend returns multiple options all with auto=true (e.g. multiple credentials for the same host), none would be auto-selected. This is likely intentional but the divergence between backend semantics and this guard is worth documenting in the JSDoc.

The credential status badge in repositories.js and project-detail.js uses emoji 🔑 as the visual indicator. The aria-label ('Credential configured') provides screen-reader accessibility, but emoji rendering may vary cross-platform. A CSS icon or text label ('Set') would be more consistent — flagging this per Developer handoff note.

[documentation-forward] api.repositories.updateCredential JSDoc mentions passing '' to clear but the QA pipeline confirmed that calling with undefined silently strips the credentialId key. The JSDoc @param for credentialId should explicitly say 'must be a string (pass empty string to clear); undefined is not supported and will produce an empty request body'.

[documentation-forward] buildCredentialSection in repository-detail.js: the auto-select guard (options.length === 1 && options[0].auto) intentionally does not fire when multiple options have auto=true. This boundary condition is undocumented. Add a JSDoc inline comment above the autoOption assignment explaining: 'Auto-select only fires when exactly one option is returned with auto=true; multiple auto-matches intentionally leave the selection on None so the user must choose explicitly'.

[documentation-forward] normalise.js: the module-level JSDoc lists the return shape of normaliseRepo() as returning credentialId: string|undefined, but LastRefreshedAt retains its Go-capitalised casing in the returned object (a deliberate asymmetry). The JSDoc return shape should note this inconsistency, e.g. add a comment 'Note: LastRefreshedAt intentionally retains Go casing to match existing consumers'.
